question: For $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, find $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$ and verify that it is perpendicular to both vectors.
explanation:
Step 1: Evaluation of the cross product
\(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&2&-1\\2&-1&1\end{vmatrix}\)
Expanding the determinant gives
\(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-5\hat{k}\)
Step 2: Perpendicularity to $\vec{a}$
\(\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})=1-6+5=0\)
Step 3: Perpendicularity to $\vec{b}$
\(\vec{b}\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})=2+3-5=0\)
Step 4: Conclusion
A zero scalar product confirms perpendicularity.
Final Answer
$\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$, and it is perpendicular to both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.

options.A: $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$, and it is perpendicular to both vectors.
options.B: $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$, and its scalar product with both vectors is zero.
options.D: $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$, and it is parallel to both vectors.
